column4: Harappan (Indus Valley) cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa flourish
Early Vedic period begins in northern India
Later Vedic period; iron begins to be used in the Ganga plains
Sixteen Mahajanapadas; Gautama Buddha and Mahavira teach (6th c. BCE)
Persian emperor Darius I conquers the Indus region
Alexander defeats Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes
Chandragupta Maurya founds the Maurya Empire with Kautilya's help
Kalinga war; Ashoka turns to Buddhism and dhamma
Pushyamitra Shunga ends Maurya rule
Sangam age in the Tamil country (c. 300 BCE to 300 CE)
Start of the Shaka era, India's national calendar era (c. 78 CE)
Kanishka's Kushana empire; Gandhara art and Mahayana Buddhism spread (c. 127 CE)
Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire
Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) rules; Kalidasa's age
Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya, with zero as a place value and the Earth's rotation
Varahamihira completes the Pancha-Siddhantika on astronomy
Harshavardhana becomes king of Kannauj
Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang begins his journey to India
Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas of Badami defeats Harsha; Aihole inscription
Rashtrakutas under Dantidurga overthrow the Badami Chalukyas
Adi Shankaracharya born (c. 788 CE) and revives Advaita Vedanta
Mahmud of Ghazni raids the subcontinent; the Chola empire is at its height
Rajaraja Chola completes the Brihadeeswarar temple at Thanjavur
Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana builds the Belur and later Halebidu temples
Basavanna, founder of the Lingayat/Veerashaiva movement, is born (c. 1131-1196)
First Battle of Tarain; Prithviraj Chauhan defeats Muhammad Ghori
Second Battle of Tarain; Ghori defeats Prithviraj Chauhan
Qutb-ud-din Aibak founds the Delhi Sultanate (Slave dynasty)
Qutub Minar construction begins in Delhi
Khalji dynasty begins under Jalaluddin Khalji
Muhammad bin Tughlaq becomes Sultan of Delhi
Harihara and Bukka found the Vijayanagara Empire on the Tungabhadra
Timur invades India and sacks Delhi
Guru Nanak born at Talwandi
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut by sea
Portuguese capture Goa under Afonso de Albuquerque
Krishnadevaraya becomes emperor of Vijayanagara
First Battle of Panipat; Babur founds the Mughal Empire
Battle of Khanwa; Babur defeats Rana Sanga
Sher Shah Suri defeats Humayun at Chausa and later founds the Suri empire
Second Battle of Panipat; Akbar secures the Mughal throne
Battle of Talikota; Vijayanagara is defeated by the Deccan sultanates
Battle of Haldighati; Rana Pratap resists Akbar
English East India Company chartered on 31 December
Shivaji born at Shivneri fort
Mumtaz Mahal dies; the Taj Mahal is begun by Shah Jahan
Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad
Aurangzeb dies; the Mughal empire starts to decline
Nadir Shah invades Delhi and takes the Peacock Throne
Battle of Plassey; British East India Company gains Bengal
Third Battle of Panipat; Marathas defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali
Battle of Buxar
First Anglo-Mysore War begins under Haidar Ali
Tipu Sultan becomes ruler of Mysore after Haidar Ali's death
Tipu Sultan dies defending Srirangapatna (4 May); Mysore passes to the Wodeyars
Third Anglo-Maratha War ends; Peshwa rule ends
Rani Chennamma of Kittur leads a revolt against the British
Sati abolished by Lord William Bentinck with Raja Ram Mohan Roy's support
Macaulay's Minute on education introduces English in schools
First train runs from Bombay to Thane (16 April)
Revolt of 1857 begins at Meerut on 10 May
Government of India Act: the Crown takes over from the East India Company
Rabindranath Tagore born (7 May)
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi born at Porbandar (2 October)
Indian National Congress founded (28 December)
Swami Vivekananda speaks at the Parliament of the World's Religions, Chicago (11 September)
Partition of Bengal (16 October); Swadeshi movement begins
All-India Muslim League founded (30 December)
Delhi Durbar; capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi
Gandhiji returns to India from South Africa (9 January)
Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League
Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar (13 April)
Non-Cooperation Movement begins (1 August)
Chauri Chaura incident; Gandhiji suspends Non-Cooperation (5 February)
Simon Commission appointed; boycott follows
Lala Lajpat Rai dies after a lathi charge (17 November)
Lahore Congress demands Purna Swaraj (December)
Dandi March / Salt Satyagraha (12 March to 6 April)
Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru hanged (23 March)
Government of India Act, 1935
Quit India Movement launched (8 August)
Subhas Chandra Bose forms the Provisional Government of Free India (21 October)
Cabinet Mission; Constituent Assembly meets (9 December)
India becomes independent (15 August); Partition of the subcontinent
Mahatma Gandhi assassinated (30 January)
Constituent Assembly adopts the Constitution (26 November)
Constitution of India comes into force (26 January); India becomes a republic
First Five-Year Plan begins; first general election in 1951-52
Andhra State formed; demand for linguistic states grows
States Reorganisation Act: states formed on linguistic lines (1 November); Mysore State enlarged
Goa, Daman and Diu liberated from Portugal (19 December)
India-China war
India-Pakistan war
ISRO founded (15 August)
Bangladesh Liberation War; Bangladesh is born (16 December)
Mysore State renamed Karnataka (1 November)
India's first nuclear test at Pokhran (18 May)
Aryabhata, India's first satellite, launched (19 April)
India win the Cricket World Cup at Lord's (25 June)
Rakesh Sharma becomes the first Indian in space (3 April)
Economic liberalisation begins under P. V. Narasimha Rao
Pokhran-II nuclear tests (11 May)
Right to Information Act passed (15 June)
Chandrayaan-1 launched (22 October); finds water molecules on the Moon
Right to Education Act passed (26 August)
Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) launched (5 November)
Mangalyaan enters Mars orbit on its first try (24 September)
ISRO launches 104 satellites on one rocket (15 February)
Chandrayaan-2 launched (22 July)
Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole (23 August)
Writing begins in Sumer (cuneiform) and Egypt (hieroglyphs)
Great Pyramid of Giza built for Pharaoh Khufu
Code of Hammurabi written in Babylon
First recorded ancient Olympic Games in Greece
Traditional founding of Rome
Roman Republic established
Battle of Marathon: Athens defeats Persia
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
Qin Shi Huang unifies China
Julius Caesar assassinated (15 March)
Augustus becomes the first Roman emperor
Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Prophet Muhammad born at Mecca (c. 570)
The Hijra; start of the Islamic calendar
Charlemagne crowned Emperor in Rome (25 December)
Norman Conquest: Battle of Hastings (14 October)
Magna Carta sealed (15 June)
The Black Death reaches Europe
Fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans (29 May)
Columbus reaches the Americas (12 October)
Martin Luther begins the Reformation (31 October)
Magellan's expedition completes the first circumnavigation
Spanish Armada defeated
Glorious Revolution in England
American Declaration of Independence (4 July)
French Revolution begins; storming of the Bastille (14 July)
Battle of Waterloo (18 June)
American Civil War begins (12 April)
Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation (1 January)
First World War begins (28 July)
Russian Revolution (7 November)
First World War ends (11 November)
Wall Street Crash begins the Great Depression (24 October)
Second World War begins (1 September)
Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Second World War ends; United Nations founded (24 October)
Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted (10 December)
Martin Luther King Jr. gives his "I have a dream" speech (28 August)
Fall of the Berlin Wall (9 November)
Dissolution of the Soviet Union (26 December)
Nelson Mandela becomes President of South Africa (10 May)
Archimedes discovers the principle of buoyancy (c. 250 BCE)
Eratosthenes measures the Earth's circumference
Ptolemy writes the Almagest
Al-Khwarizmi writes the book that gives algebra its name (c. 820)
Ibn al-Haytham writes the Book of Optics (c. 1011)
Gutenberg builds the printing press (c. 1440)
Copernicus publishes On the Revolutions; Vesalius publishes his anatomy of the human body
First compound microscope built in the Netherlands (c. 1590)
Galileo points his telescope at the sky; Kepler publishes his first two laws
William Harvey describes blood circulation
Robert Hooke names the "cell" in Micrographia
Isaac Newton publishes the Principia (5 July)
Linnaeus publishes Systema Naturae, classifying living things
Benjamin Franklin shows lightning is electrical (June)
Priestley isolates oxygen (1 August)
Edward Jenner gives the first smallpox vaccine (14 May)
Alessandro Volta invents the battery
Michael Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species (24 November)
Gregor Mendel presents his laws of heredity
Mendeleev publishes the periodic table (6 March)
Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone (7 March)
Thomas Edison demonstrates a practical electric lamp (October)
Rontgen discovers X-rays (8 November)
J. J. Thomson discovers the electron
Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium
Max Planck introduces the quantum idea
Einstein's miracle year: special relativity, E = mc^2, photoelectric effect
Bakelite, the first plastic, is made
Rutherford proposes the nucleus of the atom
Einstein publishes general relativity (November)
Alexander Fleming notices penicillin (September)
C. V. Raman discovers the Raman effect (28 February)
James Chadwick discovers the neutron
Watson and Crick describe the DNA double helix (28 February)
Sputnik 1 launched (4 October)
Yuri Gagarin is the first human in space (12 April)
Apollo 11: Neil Armstrong walks on the Moon (20 July)
First microprocessor, the Intel 4004
Hubble Space Telescope launched (24 April)
Tim Berners-Lee puts the first website online (6 August)
Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, announced (22 February)
Human Genome Project completed (April)
Higgs boson discovery announced at CERN (4 July)
LIGO detects gravitational waves (14 September)
